title: Integral Verdier biduality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work on the small pro-etale site with the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ and $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)=D(\widehat R_X)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the derived-complete integral category $D^b_c(X,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and its uniform finite-Tor subcategory $D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and let $\operatorname{Res}_n$ be derived restriction of scalars [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars].

Let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism and let $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_{X,n}^!A_n$ be its finite pro-etale dualizing object at coefficient level $n$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and let $\omega_{X,R}$ be the derived-complete integral dualizing object with its reductions $\omega_{X,R}\otimes_R^L A_n\cong\omega_{X,n}$ [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Set
$$
D_{X,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,\omega_{X,R}),\qquad
D_{X,n}M=R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(M,\omega_{X,n}),
$$
using the ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$, and $D_{X,R}$ restricts to an exact contravariant anti-equivalence of this category. For every $K$ in it the canonical evaluation-defined reduction comparisons are isomorphisms, and the output is reconstructed from those reductions:
$$
(D_{X,R}K)\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,n}K_n,
\qquad
D_{X,R}K\cong R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_nD_{X,n}K_n.
$$
Here $\otimes_R^L A_n$ means the displayed derived reduction over $\widehat R_X$. The second formula means the derived-completeness Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-complete], with reduction maps to the finite duals identified by the first comparisons and transition maps induced by finite evaluation and the dualizing reduction maps. In accordance with [def-weil-derived-limit], it asserts reconstruction as a derived limit; it does not specify an isomorphism to an independently chosen model of that limit.

For an integer $d\geq0$, if $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and all $K_n$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for integers $a\leq b$, all reductions of $D_{X,R}K$ have Tor amplitude in $[-b-2d,-a]$. The first comparisons preserve evaluation and its transposes. In particular they identify the reduction of the actual evaluation-defined double-dual map
$$
\delta_K:K\longrightarrow D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K
$$
with the finite double-dual map $\delta_{K_n}$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. The map $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K$.

proof.text: Use integral_residue_tor to identify the two integral object predicates. Map the base-field prime unit to all residue fields. Choose the coherent normalized source and finite signed presentations.

The existing ambient Hom Roos transport proves completeness, via the actual/legacy completeness equivalence. Invertibility of the normalized finite Hom comparisons gives the dualizing comparisons after mapping the specified r_n.

Choose a dimension bound. At every finite level apply finite intrinsic Verdier bounds and transfer constructibility, Tor and support through the comparison isomorphism. This proves preservation in the actual integral category.

The evaluation equation follows directly from inverse transposition and counit naturality; the arbitrary-transpose equation follows from both adjunction naturalities and tensorator naturality. Apply the coefficient pairing lemma for transition and delta compatibility. Transport the actual Roos triangle along the restricted comparison isomorphisms, checking the first legs and transition squares.

The ringed internal-Hom exactness theorem supplies the contravariant shift and distinguished-triangle preservation. First-input evaluation naturality and swap naturality prove delta naturality by equality of transposes.

Apply finite geometric biduality at every reduction. The reduction-pairing equation and invertible Hom comparisons show every reduction of delta is invertible. A distinguished cone is complete by triangulated closure. Each reduction of the cone is zero by exactness. The complete cone is zero since its Roos triangle has both product vertices zero. Thus delta is invertible.

Restrict delta to the integral constructible full subcategory. Its natural isomorphism Id ~= D.rightOp followed by D makes D faithful, then full by cancellation, and essentially surjective since each object is isomorphic to its double dual. This yields the claimed actual-dual anti-equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs, using the existing normalized Hom comparison and four genuine finite/structural compatibility results. Complete-cone conservativity is proved directly from the recorded Roos triangle.

blueprint_update.statement:
Set

$$
D_{X,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,\omega_{X,R}).
$$

This is an exact contravariant anti-equivalence of
$D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$. Its canonical comparisons satisfy

$$
(D_{X,R}K)\otimes_R^L A_n\cong D_{X,n}K_n,
\qquad D_{X,R}K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{X,n}K_n.
$$

If $\dim X\leq d$ and the reductions of $K$ have Tor interval
$[a,b]$, those of $D_{X,R}K$ have interval
$[-b-2d,-a]$. The comparisons preserve evaluation and identify
the reduction of the actual double-dual map
$\delta_K:K\to D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K$ with $\delta_{K_n}$.
In particular $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
The dualizing object and its reductions are
[prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Apply
[lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]; it proves both displayed
identifications and completeness of the ambient internal Hom.
By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], all input reductions are
finite-Tor constructible. The finite bound
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] and the comparison
[lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] prove constructibility
and the uniform interval stated for every reduction of the output.
This establishes preservation in the actual integral category.

Apply the internal-Hom comparison twice. Its evaluation
compatibility identifies the reduction of $\delta_K$, defined by
the tensor–Hom evaluation as in [lem-weil-duality-pairing],
with the canonical finite double-dual map. Those maps are
isomorphisms by [thm-fix-general-biduality].
The cone of $\delta_K$ is derived complete
([def-pe-derived-complete]) and all its reductions are zero, so it is zero
by derived Nakayama ([det-pe-derived-nakayama-first-reduction]).
Thus $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism. The evaluation identity
$D_{X,R}(\delta_K)\circ\delta_{D_{X,R}K}=\operatorname{id}$
shows that these natural isomorphisms exhibit the stated
anti-equivalence. The argument proves a property of ambient
internal Hom, not a replacement definition of that functor.
